final.title: Check the process before you automate it
final.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, ask a simpler question first: is the workflow stable enough to deserve automation at all?

For a small business owner, this usually means one repeatable task such as customer questions, invoices, or data work. If the manual version still changes from week to week, automation will not clean that up. It will just repeat the inconsistency faster. Efficient chaos is still chaos.

The practical test is not “can software do this?” but “can I describe this process clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and get the same result?” If the answer is no, the next move is not to automate first. It is to make the process visible.

Document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human must still check the work. That gives you a real basis for deciding whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. Bareni’s diagnostic starts with that kind of workflow review: one recurring process, honest about where it breaks, and kept within human approval boundaries.

final.title: Check the process before you automate it
final.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, decide whether the workflow itself is stable enough to deserve one. For an owner-operator, that means picking one repeatable task — customer questions, invoices, or data work — and asking a simple question: does it produce the same kind of output most times, or do people handle exceptions differently each week?

If the manual process is already inconsistent, automation will only repeat the inconsistency faster. The better check is more basic: can you describe the task clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and get the same result?

That is why the first step is to document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human still needs to check the work. If you can’t write that down cleanly, the workflow is not ready for automation yet.

Bareni’s diagnostic starts there: identify one recurring workflow, be honest about whether AI fits, and only then decide whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. The paper version usually tells you where the process breaks before software does.
